newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish financials catch light on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Finnish financials catch light on merger talk.

text.p: Shares in Finnish financial companies joined sharp gains in banking group Merita as brokers said talk had turned to a speculative focus on a possible link for Merita and insurer Sampo.
At 1515/1215 GMT, Merita traded at 19.10 markka, up 1.00 or over five percent in heavy volume. Sampo was also lively, at 543.00 markka, up 20.00 or nearly four percent.

"There has been talk ... of some kind of arrangement between Sampo and Merita," one broker said. Merita started the session very strong amid lively international demand and some talk of more consolidation in the Nordic financial sector.
A Merita spokeswoman said earlier there "should be nothing abnormal" in the gains, noting that Merita shares have had similar sudden gains before, last in May.
Merita's session high of 19.30 markka was a 19 percent gain on a recent June 18 trough of 16.20, and just 0.20 markka shy of its intrasession year-high of 19.50 reached on March 12.
Some analysts have target prices for Merita are between 20 and 22 markka, brokers noted. Goldman Sachs in a report earlier this week set a 1998 target of 17-22 markka.
"I suppose Merita will break through 20 markka this week and can go to 25 markka next week," one broker said.
